panels.rationale: The panel is a cross-sectional medical image (MR) of the bladder showing filling defects in the bladder wall. The article and caption confirm this finding is related to encrusted cystitis caused by Corynebacterium urealyticum.
panels.attribution_text: Ozkan et al. Encrusted cystitis caused by corynebacterium urealyticum: a case report with novel treatment strategy of intravesical dimethyl sulfoxide.. International braz j urol : official journal of the Brazilian Society of Urology 2018. doi:10.1590/s1677-5538.ibju.2017.0588. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Coronal magnetic resonance image of bladder demonstrating filling defects (arrows) of right bladder wall.
in_text_mentions: on the right bladder wall, and a moderate hydro-nephrosis at the right side was revealed with ultrasound. Filling defect at the dome and right bladder wall was also seen in magnetic resonance study (Figure-2). A diagnostic cystoscopy showed a calcified, hyperemic, fragile, edematous mucosa involving the whole bladder dome and right lateral wall covering right ureteral orifice. These lesions were completely removed with TUR, and part of the material and urine from bladder barbotage was sent for specific bacteriologic culture for Corynebacterium urealyticum, which was positive.
